_past_papers/FEE2019_recollection.pdf.label: FEE 2019 candidate recollection (Part I & II, with handwritten Part II sheets)

part1.title: Cement type for seawater / coastal exposure
part1.explain: Slag (GGBS) or pozzolanic blends reduce permeability and bind chlorides/sulfates, improving durability in marine exposure. HAC loses strength by conversion; OPC alone is more vulnerable; quick-setting cement is irrelevant.

part1.title: Effect of increasing carbon content in steel
part1.explain: More carbon → more pearlite/hardenability → higher strength and hardness but lower ductility (and weldability).

part1.title: Truss member force by joints → elongation of a rod
part1.explain: Joint E: vertical of BE = 75 kN → F_BE = 75 × 1.5/0.9 = 125 kN (T). Joint B: horizontal F_AB = 125 × 1.2/1.5 = 100 kN (T). δ = NL/(AE) = 100×10³ × 1200/(314.2 × 200 000) = 1.91 mm.

part1.title: Load sharing in a bonded RC column (compatibility)
Max BM in a beam carrying a secondary beam on rollers
part1.verify: Exact max is 1.125 kNm at 0.75 m from A (not exactly 1 kNm). Keyed (d) 'none of the above'; if the examiner only checked B, (c). Check against any official key.
part1.explain: Upper beam CD (2 m, 4 kN/m) puts 4 kN on AE at C and at the support. ΣM_A: R(4) = 4×0.5 + 4×2 + 4×4 + 5×6 = 56 → R = 14 kN, R_A = 3 kN. On AB: M = 3x − 2x² → max at x = 0.75 m = 1.125 kNm; M_B = 1.0, M_C = 0.

part1.title: Portal frame plastic collapse — beam, sway, combined
part1.explain: Beam (hinges B, load, C): P·L·θ = M(θ + 1.5θ + 0.5θ) → 3M/L. Sway (A, B, C; D pinned): P·1.5Lθ = 3Mθ → 2M/L. Combined (A, load, C): P(1.5L + L)θ = M(θ + 1.5θ + 1.5θ) → 4M/2.5L = 1.6M/L ← minimum.

part1.title: Dry unit weight & saturation from sample mass/volume
Which test gives total AND effective strength parameters
part1.explain: UCT/UU give total (undrained) only; CD gives effective only. A CU test with pore-pressure measurement gives both — not listed → (d).

part1.title: Bernoulli across a horizontal pipe reducer
Thrust on a circular gate in a 45° wall
Stepped bar: ratio of largest to smallest elongation
part1.explain: Equal lengths and force → δ ∝ 1/d². Ratio = (35/15)² = 5.44.

part1.title: Statical determinacy of three plane trusses
part1.explain: m + r vs 2j: (1) 5 + 3 = 8 = 2×4 determinate; (2) 9 + 4 = 13 > 12 indeterminate (1°); (3) 9 + 3 = 12 = 2×6 determinate (stable).

part1.title: Static indeterminacy of four beams (supports, spring, hinge)
part1.verify: Candidate recollection highlighted (c) 1,4,5,2, but counting gives beam (4) = 1. Keyed (a); confirm the support symbols on the original figure.
part1.explain: Degree = r − 3 − (internal releases). (1) pin + 2 rollers: 4 − 3 = 1. (2) fixed 3 + spring 1 + pin 2 + roller 1 = 7 − 3 = 4. (3) 3 pins 6 + fixed 3 = 9 − 3 − 1 hinge = 5. (4) pin 2 + roller 1 + spring 1 = 4 − 3 = 1.

part1.title: Force carried by reinforcement in a short column
Effect of seawater as mixing water for OPC concrete
part1.explain: Chlorides slightly accelerate early hydration but reduce long-term strength and drive reinforcement corrosion/efflorescence → reduced strength (2) and durability (4).

part1.title: Location of max upward deflection, beam with overhang
part1.explain: By moments about B, R_A = P acting downward. Between supports M = −Px, so EI·y = −Px³/6 + C₁x; y(L) = 0 → C₁ = PL²/6. Slope zero where x²/2 = L²/6 → x = L/√3 from A.

part1.title: Effective stress below a river bed
part1.explain: River depth does not matter for σ′: σ′ = (γ_sat − γ_w) z = (20 − 10) × 3 = 30 kPa (30.6 with γ_w = 9.81).

part1.title: SI: unexpected soft clay at expected pile-toe stratum
part1.explain: Boreholes for piled foundations must prove competent founding stratum to an adequate depth below the toe — continue boring until competent material is proven (and extend the investigation).

part1.title: Gauge air pressure from an inclined water column
part1.explain: Water rises 2 m along a tube at 45° to the vertical → Δh = 2cos45° = 1.414 m. p = ρgΔh = 9810 × 1.414 = 13 873 N/m².

part1.title: Froude-scaled river model velocity
Stacked blocks, top block tied — min P to slide bottom block
Find n so max span moment is at L/3 from B (overhang load nw)
part1.explain: R_B = wL/2 − nwL/18. Max where shear = 0 at R_B/w from B = L/2 − nL/18 = L/3 → n = 3.

part1.title: Velocity from a stagnation (pitot) tube rise of 1 m
Rigid bar on two aluminium posts + shorter steel post (gap)
Elastic-shortening loss when a pretensioned bar is released
Open-cut clay slope angle for FoS = 3 (Taylor's chart)
part1.explain: N_s = c_u/(F γ H) = 40/(3 × 18 × 3.7) = 0.20 → read Taylor's chart for slope angle (candidate key: 65°).

part1.title: Ingredient that increases strength (water / air / SP / silica fume)
part1.explain: Silica fume: pozzolanic + micro-filler → denser ITZ, higher strength. Water and entrained air reduce strength; SP alone only enables lower w/c.

part1.title: BCA DfMA: rank manpower savings; CLT/glulam statements
part1.explain: BCA DfMA continuum (manpower savings at project level): precast ~10% < structural steel/advanced precast ~20% < mass engineered timber ~35% < PPVC ~40%. CLT and glulam are both mass engineered timber; glulam is used mainly for beams/columns, CLT mainly for slabs/walls.

part1.title: In-situ test for undrained shear strength of clay
part1.explain: Field vane test measures c_u of soft clay directly (SPT/CPT are correlations; pressuremeter gives modulus/limit pressure).

part1.title: Falling-head permeability test (0.9 → 0.5 m in 1 h)
part1.explain: k = (aL/(At)) ln(h₁/h₂); a = π(0.003)²/4. Sample dimensions were not recalled — practise the formula.

part2.title: Strut–waler connection: web bearing & buckling of unstiffened waler web
approach: Web resistance to transverse force: EN 1993-1-5 §6 (F_Rd = f_yw L_eff t_w/γ_M1); type (c) load applied through one flange next to the diaphragm wall (or type (a) if through both flanges) — justify which.
s_s from strut flange + 20 mm end plate with 45° dispersion; k_F, F_cr = 0.9 k_F E t_w³/h_w, m₁, m₂, ℓ_y, λ̄_F, χ_F → L_eff = χ_F ℓ_y.
Compare F_Rd with 3500 kN; if inadequate: full-depth load-bearing stiffeners (EN 1993-1-5 §9.4 cruciform column check), concrete infill/packing between waler flanges, or a heavier waler.
Use UC 356×406×340 / ×235 section properties from the Blue Book (SCI P363); S355 with f_y by flange thickness (EN 10025).

part2.title: Rectangular short column: N only, then N + M (design chart)
approach: 350 × 500, f_ck = 32, f_yk = 500, 30 mm cover to links. (a) N_Rd = 0.567f_ck A_c + σ_s A_s with σ_s ≤ E_sε_c2 → A_s; check A_s,min = max(0.10N/f_yd, 0.002A_c) and A_s,max 4%.
(b) d₂/h from cover + link + ½bar; N/(bhf_ck), M/(bh²f_ck) → EC2 chart → A_s; include e₀ = max(h/30, 20) check.
Sketch bars, links φ ≥ max(6, φ_l/4), s ≤ min(20φ_l,min, b, 400) ×0.6 near slabs (EC2 9.5.3). Justify bar sizes (spacing, buildability).

key_results.note: for the 3600 kN case: 0.567 × 32 × 175 000 = 3175 kN concrete

part2.title: Bored pile in clay (α-method) + negative skin friction from fill
approach: Shaft: Q_s = Σ α c_u πd Δz (α ≈ 0.5 for bored piles in clay — state source, e.g. Tomlinson); c_u = 30 kPa (0–5 m), 40 + 3(z − 5) (5–20 m).
Base: Q_b = 9 c_u,base A_b (c_u at 20 m = 85 kPa). Subtract net pile self-weight (γ_pile − γ_soil) if asked for net capacity.
With α = 0.5: shaft 188 + 1178 = 1366 kN; base 385 kN; Q_ult ≈ 1751 kN.
(b) Fill consolidates clay → downdrag (NSF) above the neutral plane; reduces geotechnical capacity and adds structural load. Upper bound ≈ ∫ β σ′_v πd dz or α c_u along consolidating length.

part2.title: Crest & sag vertical curves (SSD) + 3-layer AASHTO flexible pavement
approach: SSD = vt + v²/(2g(f + G)): 70 km/h, t = 2.5 s, f = 0.30. Crest uses G = −3% → 120.0 m; sag uses G = −4% (approaching from the other side) → 122.7 m.
Half-lengths 90 + 96 = 186 m > 150 m tangent → curves cannot be fully developed.
Pavement: D₁ = SN₁/a₁ = 2.3/0.45 = 5.1 in; D₂ = (SN₂ − a₁D₁)/(a₂m₂) = 4.2 in; D₃ = (SN₃ − SN₂)/(a₃m₃) = 7.6 in — round up to practical/minimum thicknesses and recompute.
Flexible vs rigid: lower initial cost, staged construction, easier repair/utility access, tolerant of differential settlement, smoother riding, faster opening.

part2.title: T-shaped column: N–M interaction diagram from strain compatibility
approach: Pure axial: N = 0.567f_ck A_c,net + 0.87f_yk ΣA_s (or σ_s at ε_c2) with f_ck = 45.
Pure bending: find neutral axis by force equilibrium (λ = 0.8, η = 1.0 for f_ck ≤ 50), steel stresses from ε_cu = 0.0035.
Balanced point: x_bal from ε_cu and ε_yd = 435/200 000; tension-failure point at x = 100 mm as specified.
Take moments about the plastic centroid; plot (M, N) points and join.

part2.title: Sluice gate: specific energy, critical flow, hydraulic jump, bed slope
approach: q = 2 m²/s → y_c = (q²/g)^⅓ = 0.742 m, E_c = 1.5y_c = 1.112 m. Fr₁ = 1.81 → supercritical.
Assume y₂ is uniform (normal) depth downstream: S₀ = (nQ/(AR^⅔))² ≈ 0.0035.

part2.title: Primary clarifier sizing + sludge volume; activated sludge V, MLVSS, θc
approach: Combined Q = 520 m³/d, BOD = 611.5 mg/L → 318 kg/d; V = 318/4 = 79.5 m³; HRT = 3.67 h.
MLVSS = QS/(V·F/M) = 6667 mg/L. θc = VX/(Q_eX_e + Q_wX_r) with Q_e = 425 m³/d, X_r = 10 000 mg/L → 0.55 d.

part2.title: Braced columns from a floor plan + sub-frame moment, slenderness
approach: Set in BS 8110 terms (f_cu, f_y = 460) — legacy, not acceptable in FEE 2027. Re-do in EC2: f_ck = 28/35 equivalent, f_yk = 500.
EC2: l₀ = 0.85 × 4 m; λ = l₀/i vs λ_lim = 20ABC/√n (5.8.3.1); sub-frame moments for column B; nominal curvature if slender.

part2.title: Pile selection next to MRT viaduct; OCR of marine clay; NSF
approach: Bored vs driven RC piles: vibration/noise/heave next to MRT piles and bakau-piled shophouses favour bored piles (or jacked); address marine clay, groundwater, boulders.
Mitigation: monitoring (tiltmeters, settlement markers, vibration limits), casing, sequencing, LTA protection zone requirements.
Compare p′₀ with p′_c → NC/under-consolidated clay → NSF acts; sketch axial load with neutral plane; toe into competent stratum (Old Alluvium/Jurong).

part2.title: Plate girder: classification, M_el/M_pl/M_c,Rd, V_pl,Rd, shear flow, weld
approach: EC3 Table 5.2 classification; W_el/W_pl from built-up geometry; EN 1993-1-5 shear buckling if h_w/t_w > 72ε/η; shear flow VQ/I → fillet weld size (EC3-1-8 4.5.3.3).

part2.title: Fin plate connection
approach: SCI P358 (Green Book) checks: bolt group shear with eccentricity, bearing on plate/web, plate shear & block tearing, weld to supporting member.

part2.title: Prestressed RC beam
approach: Transfer & service stress limits, Magnel diagram, losses (elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, relaxation).

part2.title: 400×400 column design + fire resistance with 4H25 (ψ_fi = 0.3)
approach: Design A_s for N_Ed, M_Ed (γ_G 1.35, γ_Q 1.5), detail links φ8 and cover 30.
Fire: EN 1992-1-2 §5.3 tabulated data (Method A): μ_fi = N_Ed,fi/N_Rd with η_fi from ψ_fi = 0.3; compare min b and axis distance a for R60/R90/R120.

part2.title: Bored pile DA1 design resistance (α-method, ξ) + static load test
approach: c_u linear 30 → 120 kPa over 30 m; α-method shaft + 9c_u base; characteristic via ξ = 1.55 (model-pile procedure) → R_c,d with γ_s, γ_b for DA1-C2 (R4 set).
Working vs test (preliminary/ultimate) piles; characteristic from static tests: R_c,k = min(R_mean/ξ₁, R_min/ξ₂).

part2.title: 1.5 m pad on clay: influence depth, ULS DA1, consolidation settlement
approach: Influence depth where Δσ_z ≈ 0.1–0.2σ′_v0 (2:1 or Boussinesq); if within Clay 1 only, no settlement from Clay 2.
ULS: undrained (π+2)c_u s_c i_c + q and/or drained Annex D for DA1-C1 & C2.
Settlement (NC, OCR = 1): s = Σ C_c H/(1+e₀) log(σ′_f/σ′_0) in sub-layers.

part2.title: Greenshields v = 60 − 0.5k; horizontal curve concepts; 2-layer AASHTO
approach: v_f = 60 km/h, k_j = 120 veh/km → q_max = 1800 veh/h at k = 60, v = 30 km/h.
Speed-limit considerations: geometry/sight distance, crash history, roadside activity/access, 85th-percentile speed.
Horizontal curve: superelevation + side friction (R = V²/127(e+f)), transition/spiral curves, sight distance on inside of curve.

part2.title: 3 m rectangular channel (S₀ 0.002, n 0.015): y_c, E_c, y₀, jump
approach: Q not recalled — practise with the app's Manning calculator (z = 0). y_c = (q²/g)^⅓, E_c = 1.5y_c; solve y₀ by Manning; compare y₀ vs y_c.
Jump with y₂ = y₀ (weir): y₁ = (y₂/2)(√(1 + 8Fr₂²) − 1).

part2.title: Activated sludge
approach: F/M, V, HRT, MLVSS, θc — see PP2-clarifier-as for the formula set.
